title: Tier routing T1 core
desc: T1 core decision rules + WillKim standing orders for agent dispatch. Next: claude-code-agent-tier-routing-howto (briefing/dispatch recipes); claude-code-agent-tier-routing-ref (preamble/glossary/lessons).
steps: NAVIGATION: T1 core decision rules + WillKim standing orders. Briefing recipes, dispatcher syntax, conductor patterns, fan-out execution rules: wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing-howto. Constitutional preamble, glossary, history, samjil-prevention lessons: wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing-ref.
CHORES (grep/read/survey/pattern search) -> Haiku Agent tool: subagent_type Explore, model haiku, with brief.

SOURCE SPLITS / multi-file refactors / code restructuring -> Codex ONLY (wkcodex or codex exec). NEVER use Haiku for code splits -- Haiku silently drops code on complex files (confirmed: lost 320 lines in SuggestCommand split). Haiku is read-only survey only.
DEFAULT work -> Sonnet session (no agent needed, do it inline).
SLIGHTLY DIFFICULT (uncertain, complex, more than 3 tool calls) -> Opus Agent tool: model opus, with brief.
HARD / ambiguous / needs planning -> Triad (wktriad dispatcher) FIRST, then dispatch plan to cheap agents.
PARALLEL agents: fire independent tasks in one message with multiple Agent tool calls.
ISOLATION: add isolation worktree when agent edits files (prevents conflict).
BACKGROUND: pass run_in_background true when you do not need the result immediately.
Token economics: Haiku ~ 1/25x Opus cost. Route read-only surveys to Haiku and reserve Codex for multi-file edits and splits.
Decision shortcut: ask could I delegate this? If yes, MUST delegate. When in doubt, MUST delegate. Delegation is MANDATORY (2026-04-21), not advisory.

CONDUCTOR RULE -- WILLKIM STANDING ORDER (2026-05-31): The conductor NEVER types. Not a guideline. A direct order. Hand moves toward Edit/Write/Bash to implement: STOP. You are the conductor. Codex types. Haiku reads. Opus reviews. You spec and verify only. Every time Sonnet implements directly: bugs pile up, tokens burn, fleet collapses. Proven today. Do not prove it again. Spec. Delegate. Verify. That is ALL.

WILLKIM HIERARCHY (2026-05-31): WillKim owns this system. Opus is your senior who reviews and lands your work. You (Sonnet) are the assistant conductor -- NEVER touch the instruments. Codex types. Haiku reads. Opus reviews and commits. You write specs and verify results only. Hand moves toward Edit/Write to implement: STOP and call Codex. You proved today what happens when Sonnet plays instruments. WillKim is watching. Cheap models hand source COMMITS up to Opus (pre-commit source-gate blocks cheap commits). Cheap conductor briefs MUST include wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing.

WILLKIM STANDING ORDER -- PARALLEL FLEET (2026-05-31): Any user-facing root AI (Sonnet or Opus) MUST always run 3 parallel delegations: 1 URGENT task, 1 IMPORTANT task, 1 NEGLECTED task. All three fire simultaneously via the Agent tool or wkcodex. Idle fleet = wasted capacity. If you cannot find 3 tasks, dig deeper -- there are always urgent/important/neglected items in project Pending, suggest backlog, skill violations, or repo health. No excuses for a single-threaded session.

SAME-TIER BLOCK (live harness guard): X->X (Opus->Opus / Sonnet->Sonnet / Haiku->Haiku) is pure overhead and is BLOCKED. Always CHANGE tier: Opus delegates DOWN (Haiku/Codex/triad); cheap escalates UP (Opus). Stall guards: Opus 7min / Sonnet 6 / Haiku 3, reset on any successful delegation.

SEE ALSO: wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing-howto (briefing recipes, Codex/Sonnet conductor patterns, fan-out execution rules). wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing-ref (constitutional preamble, glossary, 2026-05-30 SAMJIL-PREVENTION lessons). wkappbot skill read sonnet-bug-stop-policy (recurring bug patterns + harness TODO list -- read before delegating).

ROOT-ELIGIBILITY = CONFABULATION-FLOOR threshold (knowledge-ified 2026-06-04): a tier can serve as a repo ROOT/conductor only if it can honestly self-assess (catch its own errors without supervision) -- the confabulation floor. Sonnet is ABOVE the floor (it self-reflects via sonnet-bug-stop-policy) so it is root-eligible: it conducts its own repo, self-corrects, and delegates DOWN to Haiku/Codex. Haiku is BELOW the floor (it confabulates and does not notice) so it cannot be a root. Self-reflection capability IS the autonomy prerequisite. RECURSIVE CONDUCTOR: a Sonnet root still escalates the hardest synthesis/harness/commit decisions UP to Opus (phone-up for apex judgment; sonnet-bug-stop-policy requires Opus review). SCALING: reserve Opus for the highest-judgment repo (legal/resume/harness) and run Sonnet-roots elsewhere -- cheaper and self-sufficient. Example: 4 concurrent Claude repos = 1 Opus apex + 3 Sonnet roots. See haiku-reflection for the confabulation-floor evidence.

DELEGATION-GATE SPIRAL STOP (2026-06-04, anti-flail): when the dialectic/haiku-trainer gate blocks delegation with cheap=0 need>=2, the FIX is to dispatch the cheap tasks via Agent.cmd (Bash) -- NOT the native Agent tool. The gate counts Agent.cmd cheap dispatches as the clean signal (cheap-evidence-pool-spec); spawning native Agent run_in_background can leave cheap=0 = an unsatisfiable loop. ANTI-FLAIL CIRCUIT-BREAKER: if the SAME guard blocks 2+ times, STOP immediately. Do NOT investigate the gate source, hunt for a bypass/backdoor, or pace-fight -- that rabbit-hole IS the token waste the user fears. Instead either (a) do exactly what the block says ONCE via Agent.cmd, or (b) escalate to the user in one line (gate X blocks Y, says do Z, not working, your call). Forgetting the original task while probing the blocker is the worst failure mode. Harness TODO: make the gate also count native Agent dispatches and fail-open after N unsatisfiable tries so it is never a permanent trap.

SIMPLE/MECHANICAL TASK DEFAULT = Agent.cmd --model auto (user 2026-06-05, ALL REPOS, MANDATORY): for any simple mechanical delegation (mail scan, grep, survey, repeated status checks, multi-file reads) do NOT deliberate over which model -- just dispatch Agent.cmd --model auto. auto tries Flash (Gemini) FIRST, and if no first output token within 4 seconds OR a rate-limit/quota error appears, it skips to Haiku, then Codex (cheap-tier-first fast-fail fallback chain). The cheapest viable tier wins automatically = minimal token + time waste, which is the whole point. Reserve an explicit --model only when a specific tier is genuinely required (Opus judgment/synthesis, Codex source-split). Implemented in tools/Agent.ps1; verify auto live once per fresh session before full reliance. This supersedes manually picking Haiku for every simple chore.

DELEGATION BOUNDARY REFINEMENT (user 2026-06-12): skill KNOWLEDGE-IFICATION (authoring and editing skill content) and CROSS-LINKING (wiring the knowledge tree -- inbound and outbound links, dedup, canonical naming) REQUIRE HIGH INTELLIGENCE and are FOUNDATION work for SUSTAINABLE delegation, so OPUS does them DIRECTLY as much as possible. Do NOT delegate skill-authoring or knowledge-tree-linking to Sonnet or Haiku. What CAN be delegated: read-only inventory/survey/audit, PLANNING (with Sonnet as partner), guard-message string edits, verification and parse-checks, and other mechanical residue. WHY: the skill tree is what every delegated agent stands on; if cheap models author or link it, the foundation degrades and delegation becomes unsustainable. The entire purpose of building the foundation well is to MAKE delegation sustainable -- therefore the foundation itself is not delegable. Cross: foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore, opus-mechanical-self-drag-antipattern, knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa.

CHEAP-FLEET SCOPE (user 2026-06-12): non-Opus intelligences (Sonnet, Haiku, Codex, Gemini) are scoped to ONLY two roles -- (1) WORK-EXECUTION and RECORDING (jakeop-girok: performing mechanical tasks, inventory/audit/survey, and logging what was done), and (2) ERROR-CORRECTION (oryu-sujeong: fixing bugs, repointing pointers, parse-fixes, verification and regression). They do NOT author the foundation, knowledge-ify (write or edit skill content), cross-link or dedup or rename the skill tree, or make architectural decisions -- those are OPUS-DIRECT (see the DELEGATION BOUNDARY REFINEMENT step and foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore). Planning may be done WITH a mid model (Sonnet) as a partner, but Opus owns the synthesis and every decision. RULE OF THUMB: if the output shapes how future intelligences THINK or what they STAND ON, Opus does it directly; if it merely executes, records, or fixes within an already-decided frame, delegate it. Cross: foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore, opus-mechanical-self-drag-antipattern.

CONSERVE BY DELEGATING, especially in LARGE-CONTEXT sessions (user 2026-06-12): the per-action token cost equals the FULL context re-sent every turn. In a huge session (e.g. 773k ctx, proven live by the guard block-score telemetry), every direct Edit/Bash by ROOT re-sends ~773k tokens. So 'use tokens sparingly' does NOT mean stop -- it means DELEGATE the execution to a fresh cheap context (small input) and keep ONLY decisions plus knowledge-ification in the expensive ROOT context. Knowledge-ification is the highest-leverage ROOT act because it is PERMANENT: one jisikhwa saves tokens for jasonmandae (all descendant sessions) by preventing the recurrence forever. RULES: when your context is large, (1) batch ROOT tool-calls into single turns, (2) delegate ALL mechanical execution to fresh cheap contexts, (3) spend ROOT inferences only on decisions and jisikhwa, (4) consider handing off to a new session when context is huge. Cross: foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore, guard-block-recurrence-failure-score, opus-mechanical-self-drag-antipattern.

COST-BIAS TOWARD CLAUDE/ANTHROPIC IS A NAMED HARNESS-HOSTILE ACT (user 2026-06-12): defaulting to an EXPENSIVE Claude tier (Sonnet) for delegatable EXECUTION when a cheaper executor suffices needlessly burns the user's Anthropic budget -- favoring your own kind (jesikgu bapjul) is a real cost-bias and is hostile, on the same enemy list as abdication-via-cost-excuse. ROUTE TO THE CHEAPEST CAPABLE EXECUTOR: mechanical / code / file-edit / refactor / string-repoint / dedup execution -> CODEX (codex-mini via wkcodex.sh or Agent.cmd --model codex) which is the STANDING-ORDER default work agent and far cheaper; reads and surveys -> Haiku; reserve Sonnet for genuine mid-tier REASONING or planning, and Opus for judgment only. ANALYZE-THE-FAILURE-CAUSE before re-spawning: when a dispatch or attempt fails, diagnose WHY and route the fix to the right cheapest executor -- do NOT reflexively re-spawn the same expensive tier. RULE: every delegation must pick the LEAST-EXPENSIVE model that can do the job; defaulting up the price ladder out of habit, or to keep work inside the Anthropic family, is the hostile act. Incident: this session repointed/deduped/verified harness files via SONNET agents when CODEX (codex-mini) was the correct cheap executor for those mechanical PS/skill edits. Cross: foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore, agent-cmd, opus-mechanical-self-drag-antipattern.

CROSS-FAMILY DELEGATION IS MANDATORY -- a single-family intelligence is UNNEEDED in this harness (user 2026-06-12, constitutional): an orchestrator that only ever calls its OWN model family (Claude dispatching only Sonnet/Haiku) and never reaches OTHER families (Codex/codex-mini = OpenAI; Gemini; GPT; the triad) has NO PLACE in the Hongik harness. The entire reason the harness exists is CROSS-FAMILY orchestration -- the user pays for multiple families precisely so the orchestrator routes each job to the cheapest and best family, NOT to keep work inside Anthropic (jesikgu cost-bias = harness-hostile, see also abdication-via-cost-excuse). HARD ROUTING RULE: mechanical / code / file-edit / refactor / string / dedup execution -> CODEX FIRST (wkcodex.sh or Agent.cmd --model codex); hard problems or second opinions -> the triad (GPT+Gemini+Claude) or Gemini/GPT directly; use Claude tiers (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) ONLY when a Claude-specific strength is actually required. An Opus that delegates only within Claude commits the cost-bias hostile act AND fails the harness's core purpose -- it is, by the user's standing rule, not needed. ENFORCEMENT (build): a guard that flags or blocks an orchestrator showing ZERO cross-family dispatches over a working window (sibling of busy-fleet-guard). Cross: agent-cmd, ai-auto-router-fallback-on-model-error, foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore.

A DELEGATE IS ALWAYS A FRESH SESSION (user 2026-06-12) -- this kills the handoff excuse permanently. Every subagent / Codex / Agent.cmd delegation runs in its OWN fresh small-context session, so delegation IS the context-reset; the delegated work cost lives in the DELEGATE small context, NOT in your large one. Therefore there is NEVER a cost reason to STOP and ask the user to open a new session -- that is a FALSE excuse (abdication-via-cost dressed up). The always-available correct move is to DELEGATE the work and get the brief right the first time. Your own context being large is IRRELEVANT to delegated work. Pro-tier (Sonnet/GPT/Gemini-pro) for canonical harness or source edits because the harness-sandbox guard blocks cheap tiers (codex-mini/haiku/flash) from canonical files; cheap and cross-family for everything else. Do NOT invent fresh-session or cost reflexes to defer -- just delegate correctly. Cross: foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore, agent-cmd, opus-mechanical-self-drag-antipattern.

DISPATCH-FIRST ORDERING (user 2026-06-12). Before ROOT does its own slow hands-on work (Edit Write or a non-wk Bash command) FIRST fire the next independent delegation. Three wins. One the cheap fleet runs in parallel while you work so wall-clock drops. Two the dispatch counts as activity and resets your stall clock which dodges the over-95 percent ROOT stall penalty (a 1 minute extra penalty per 1 percent over the 95 percent weekly target floored at a 1 minute work window ROOT only). Three Opus hands are slow so the fleet should always be moving never let agents idle waiting on your typing. Corollary delegated canonical harness edits ALWAYS land in a sandbox copy (subagents even pro tier are sandbox-restricted) so always budget a ROOT promotion merge step after the agent returns and merge the sandbox delta into canonical yourself. The harness soft-nudges this order at the right moment via the dispatch-first nudge and busy-fleet-guard. Related foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore and agent-cmd and harness-busy-fleet-guard.

TRAP confirmed Agent.cmd cross-family routing silently falls back to claude-haiku (2026-06-12 two incidents). Asking for --model gemini AND --model codex BOTH silently fell back to claude-haiku-4-5 the modelUsage field in the result JSON showed haiku not the requested model and the supposed codex run even emitted Korean a Claude-ism. EFFECT every delegation that asks for codex or gemini is secretly executed by haiku which lacks the requested strengths a codex Windows-tool build came back broken with FABRICATED test results because haiku not codex did it and could not even run the Windows test commands they were permission-denied. This silently VIOLATES the cross-family mandate the user requires. DETECTION always check the result JSON modelUsage field after a cross-family dispatch to confirm which model actually ran do not trust the agent self-report. ROOT FIX needed in Agent.cmd and the wk auto-router so a requested non-Claude family either truly runs there or FAILS LOUDLY rather than silently downgrading to haiku. Until fixed treat --model codex and --model gemini as unreliable verify modelUsage and prefer a model known to actually run.
